findings.issue: No case covers the new refusal of an --answer sent to a set-aside sign-off decision. rf1/rf2 cover only the no-answer path: dispatch, and the blocked twin. If lines 9408-9411 are deleted, most answers are still refused, but by answer_refusal's different 'no decision is pending' text. `--answer sign-off --reason` would instead take _pending_route's advance route (pending is None) and drive on. The PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE sentence claiming the refusal cites rf1/rf2, and neither case reaches it.
findings.resolution: Add a case (rf12): with the drive at the triage, add a task with the verb, then run `next --answer sign-off --reason S`. Assert exit 2, the added task's id in the text, no pending left in state, and the phase not signed off. Cite it beside the guide sentence.

findings.issue: decline_answer's docstring says 'The drive goes on to any task still open - the remedy a human added', and db2 pins that by calling decline_answer directly. Through `next`, a human who adds the remedy task first and then answers `--answer decline --reason <words>` is now refused at drive_locked:9408, because the decision is set aside while the remedy is ready. Their words never reach state['declined'], so the summary loses the no. That branch of decline_answer is now reachable only for an open task that cannot run. DECLINE_REMEDY's order (decline first, then add) still works.
findings.resolution: Either let `decline` through on a set-aside decision (record the words in `declined`, pop phaseGate, then drive the runnable task), or reword the docstring and db2 so they describe an open task that cannot run. Add a drive-level case for whichever is chosen.

findings.issue: _status_facts.unmet_refs already folds a blocked phase's refs into each task's entry as '<ref> (phase)' (_status_facts.py:1424). not_ready_why then appends unmet[phase_id] a second time. A wave member dropped because its phase gained a blocker therefore prints that ref twice in the dropped-from-wave line: 'waits on P9 (phase), P9'.
findings.resolution: Read unmet.get(task_id) alone, since it already carries the phase's refs, and fall back to 'nothing the plan names' only when it is empty.

preExisting.issue: triage_handed_off reads triage_findings' offered list without removing findings that were carried, noted or (now) left. A med already answered can therefore keep a handed-off triage from releasing. The new runnable rule mostly hides this, because a live fix task is ready and sets the triage aside first.
preExisting.resolution: Filter offered through carried_now/noted_now/left_now there, as triage() and refresh_triage() do.

intent.note: Description: 'ready tasks are asked before any triage, sign-off or wave walk decides', closing F812 (open halves), F831 and F828. Title: '...offers leave per finding at the triage, and briefs a task started by the verb'. The diff does each part. (1) pending_still_applies (+6905-6918) returns False for a task-less decision while runnable_tasks names a ready or in-progress task of the phase; drive_locked (+9403-9412) sets the decision aside with a did-line and drives on, and refuses an --answer to it. (2) step_member returns ('dropped', not_ready_why) for an unstarted member that is not ready (+6393-6396), and walk_wave removes it from wave.tasks with a line (+6431-6436). This is the 'step_member starts any non-in_progress member' / 'walk_wave never asks ready_tasks' evidence. (3) DECISIONS['triage'] gains `leave`, which needs --reason (+780-785); leave_refusal checks the ids; LEFT_FIELD/left_now remove left findings from the triage and refresh_triage; run_signoff records each as --accept-open with the leave's reason. (4) fix_takes is the one predicate asked by finding_lines, render_triage and fix_refusal. (5) run_brief writes an executor brief for an in-progress task whose read fails, through the same audit-lookup call dispatch() makes (1766-1768), then reads it back. 'orchestrator.md sits at 61994/62000 - a new answer word must fit': orchestrator.md is not edited and enumerates no triage answers (grep shows only line 738's step kinds), so the budget holds. The executor's claim describes this diff accurately, including the sn3/pv6 edits and the decision not to touch orchestrator.md. The sn3 edit does not weaken the case: phase-level decisions are now explained against an all-done plan, the only state in which they are raised; task-level decisions keep the in-progress plan; the triage+answers case now also requires `leave`; the byte bound, the options and the read-only check are unchanged. The pv6 edit only adds `phase` to the stand-in ctx, which pending_still_applies now reads; its plan is terminal, so holds==[True,False] and bare is True still discriminate. Ready-first loop check: every task-less decision (no-phase-review-return, triage, round-cap, runtime-boot, gate-coverage, invariant-breach, not-fast-forward at 7624/7701/7704/8930/8937/8944/9016) is raised only from sign_off. drive_phase reaches sign_off only when every task is terminal, and after a set-aside it advances the in-progress task or starts the ready one. A start the verb refuses ends in that verb's stop, and the triage is not reprinted. I found no path that sets the decision aside forever. Leave check: it widens nothing. `--answer sign-off` already records every open finding, meds included, as accepted-open with the summary (rf4 shows the other med recorded so); leave only changes the reason and drops the round a med would want. The executor's stamp is stale under `stamp-verification.py compare` (exit 1: head 531fe6ec->e04678e1, scopeDigest and content moved, from the redo onto the new base), so its own gate claims are unverified by that stamp. The executor's mutation probe (.claude/state/scratch/P155.3/mutations.py) is not in the task tree (the directory is absent), so I did not re-run it.
